title: Compact finite support in simplicial realization
statement: Let $K$ be a small simplicial set, and let $|K|$ denote its geometric realization with the quotient topology of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. A simplicial subset $A\subseteq K$ means subsets $A_n\subseteq K_n$ stable under every face and degeneracy map. Call $A$ finite if it has only finitely many nondegenerate simplices, where a simplex is nondegenerate when it is not in the image of a degeneracy map. For every compact Hausdorff topological space $T$ and every continuous map $a:T\to|K|$, there are a finite simplicial subset $A\subseteq K$ and a continuous map $a_A:T\to|A|$ such that $a=|\iota_A|\circ a_A$, with $\iota_A:A\hookrightarrow K$ the inclusion. In particular, this factorization holds for $T=S^n=\{x\in\mathbb R^{n+1}:\sum_i x_i^2=1\}$ for every integer $n\geq0$; these spheres, with their usual subspace topology, are compact Hausdorff.

source.place: WANTED: archived Kerodon, Proposition 3.6.1.11 (Kerodon Tag 0139, https://kerodon.net/tag/0139), together with the closed-embedding observation immediately before it in Subsection 3.6.1 (Kerodon Tag 0130). Checked online 2026-10-16: compact subsets lie in realizations of finite simplicial subsets, whose realization inclusions are closed embeddings. The sphere specialization uses the usual compactness of Euclidean spheres.
